A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DataGen and contain complete main texts and Appendices A–K. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and embedded screenshots support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original dataset-generation experiments, module evaluations, human evaluations, benchmarking, and data-augmentation results in Section 3 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results, including benchmarking tables, human evaluations, and downstream fine-tuning experiments.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same generation, reflection/enhancement, code-based evaluation, RAG validation, difficulty enhancement, and group-checking procedures. The prompts in Appendix I and framework in Appendix K also match.

E1.justification: The four main benchmarking datasets, downstream augmentation tasks, Alpaca/MT-Bench experiments, and single/combined user-constraint scenarios remain identical, including the Chinese and Spanish constraints.

E2.justification: The four DyVal2 principle baselines in Table 3 and base/original-Alpaca controls in Table 8 are unchanged. The evaluated LLM rosters in Tables 6, 7, and 13 also match.

E3.justification: Sample sizes, test sets, human-evaluation design, metrics, and judging procedures are unchanged. Appendix E retains generation batch size 5, inference temperature 0 and top-p 1, and the same five-epoch fine-tuning settings.

E4.justification: Both retain the same module evaluations, temperature sensitivity, human and error analyses, cost analysis, constraint tests, supplementary diversity analyses, training-loss curves, and Appendix H examples.

E5.justification: There is no addition or revision of run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or statistical tests. Appendix D retains the same averaging across five human evaluators.

E6.justification: Reported values and plotted findings match, including DataGen's 3.83% average entity overlap in Table 3, the genset MT-Bench average of 6.403 in Table 8, and supplementary results in Tables 12–14.

T1.justification: The dataset-generation formulation and embedding-distance definition in Section 2, and the SFT objective in Appendix E, Equation (1), are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified generation, diversity, truthfulness, controllability, benchmarking, and data augmentation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of benchmarking and augmentation results remain unchanged, as do Appendix A's applicability limitations and proposed improvements and Appendix G's societal-risk discussion.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, LoRA parameters, A100 hardware disclosure, framework information, prompt templates, and code-access information are identical. No reproducibility details are added or removed.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion in Appendix B, comparison in Table 1, and positioning against prior generation frameworks are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv margin stamp changes from v4, 5 June 2025, to v5, 17 November 2025. The title, visible author block, manuscript wording, and section/appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small spacing and page-break changes on pages 24–25 move an existing line to the preceding page and shift appendix displays, including Tables 13–14 and Figure 10. Figure/table content, structure, and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The updated version/date stamp and small appendix reflow leave the method, empirical evidence, claims, limitations, and reproducibility information unchanged. They produce no meaningful overall difference in scientific support or readability.
